C-INITIAL-SCHEMA-BASELINE.Summary: Retain the implemented exercise/session/set hierarchy and three-panel TUI, and replace migration history with a CLI-timestamped initial migration for the latest complete schema.

Goals.Goal: Exercise to sessions to sets hierarchy with session CRUD and UUID identifiers.
Exercises above sets on the left half; title-only sessions occupy the right half; focus shortcuts 1, 2, and 3.
Remove duplicate TUI record types and all date separators from set rendering.
Replace every existing SQLite migration with one initial up/down pair generated by golang-migrate using the current clock.

Constraints.Constraint: Initialize fresh databases with exercises, sessions, sets, preferences, identities, and credentials. Remove all previous SQL migrations. Existing databases using the old migration history are outside this new baseline; do not open, reset, or change the real user database.
Sessions require trimmed nonempty titles; duplicate titles are allowed. Default creation timestamps to UTC now. Cascade exercise and session deletion.

Preserve existing keyboard navigation, page movement without separate page indicators, border counters, dialog/setup/help input isolation, transfer ownership, and compact layouts. Mouse-wheel navigation stays disabled.
Use domain constructors, one use case per file, package errors.go files, and one argument per line for multiargument Go calls. Do not add automated test files.

Use the installed golang-migrate CLI with Europe/Moscow timezone to generate the init filenames. Preserve exactly the current six-table schema, constraints, foreign keys, indexes, and timestamp defaults.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No whole-workout sessions, session reparenting, or old-data migration. No browser, authentication, or unrelated domain redesign.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: One initial migration pair directly creates the latest schema. Sessions store id, exercise_id, title, created_at; sets reference session_id. Down drops all six application tables in dependency-safe order. All earlier migration SQL files are removed.
Session create/rename/delete/list use cases validate references and constructors. Session deletion removes its sets; deleting the last set retains its session.
Three responsive panels filter children by selected parent; refreshes retain selected IDs or clamp selection. Enter advances exercise to session to sets. n/e/d act on the active panel.
TUI state holds domain exercises, sessions, and sets. Session rows show only titles. Set rows show reps, weight, and rest without date separators. Weight conversion happens for display.
Snapshot version 2 contains sessions and validates the entire reference hierarchy. Old backups are rejected before local mutation. Restore is atomic and retains local credentials.
Build, vet, formatting, temporary-database scenarios, TUI interaction checks, and final GRACE assertions pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Temporary database comparison proves exact schema equivalence, init up/down/up, constraints, cascade behavior, timestamp defaults, and embedded migration operation; retain the already verified session/TUI implementation.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user approved session implementation, explicitly chose sequential execution, then requested squashing all migrations and confirmed golang-migrate. These instructions authorize this replacement bundle; final apply/archive confirmation remains separate.
Sessions and sets order by created_at DESC then id DESC. The left column divides usable height equally after footer reservation. Title edits retain session ownership and timestamps.
